sources.entry: Nifro - Turn websites into configurable desktop wallpapers, with separate views for each display. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/PathGao/Nifro)

summary.one_liner: Nifro is a macOS app that turns any website into a desktop wallpaper, with separate pages and controls for each display.
summary.what_it_does: Nifro displays a web page behind your windows as the Mac desktop wallpaper, such as a live camera, art site, map, dashboard, or shader. Each display can show a different page, with its own controls and state, shown side by side in a menu-bar panel. Users can drag, scroll or zoom to crop a page to the region they want, and Nifro remembers that region when a display changes size. Sites can be organized into playlists that stay on one site, cycle in order or at random, or follow each site's schedule. Holding a key lets the user click and interact with the page, and sound and link behaviour are remembered per website. A built-in gallery of desktop-suitable sites is included, and the app is available in English and Simplified Chinese.
use_cases: Set a live webcam or nature view as desktop wallpaper
Show a dashboard or usage page behind open windows
Display a live weather or flight map on the desktop
Run generative art or ambient animation as a background
Assign different web pages to each monitor
Rotate desktop backgrounds through a playlist of websites
how_to_run: Or download Nifro-arm64.dmg (Apple silicon) or Nifro-x86_64.dmg (Intel) from the releases page
git clone the repository, cd Nifro, and run ./build.sh to build a local development app
swift test to run the test suite
notable: Per-display wallpapers, controls and state, with a menu-bar panel showing all displays side by side
Crop and zoom a page to a region, preserved when moved to a display of a different size
Playlists with sequential, random, or schedule-based site rotation
Hold a key to interact with a page, then return to wallpaper mode
Rebuilt from the idea of Plash by Sindre Sorhus
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later; building from source requires Xcode 26 or later
Homebrew cask is a third-party tap that the README asks users to review before trusting
Full-screen video and macOS transitions can cause a fixed Dock to behave as auto-hide; the README says this is a known macOS bug
